sentences.text:
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, learned HCGP for respondent no.1 and learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2.
3.

FIR in Crime No.509/2023 was registered by Pulakeshinagar Police Station, Bengaluru City,
against the petitioner herein initially for the offences punishable under Sections 4, 6 & 15 of POCSO Act and Sections 376(2)(f) & 376(2)(n) of IPC, on the basis of first information dated 28.12.2023 submitted by the victim girl, who was a major.
During the course of investigation, the petitioner herein was arrested on 16.03.2024 and remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed for the aforesaid offences.
4. The bail application filed by the petitioner before the Jurisdictional Sessions Court in Crl.Misc.No.5402/2023 was rejected on 28.06.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.

2 5. Learned counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition, submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in a criminal case at the instance of the present coach of the victim girl.

She submits that even as per the prosecution case, the victim girl had attained the age of majority as on 27.04.2023 and the first information was submitted on 28.12.2023, alleging that the petitioner who was the coach of the victim from the year 2020 onwards, had committed sexual assault on her during the second week of March- 2023.
She submits that the petitioner's mother, who is a cancer patient has been undergoing treatment for her ailment for the last more than one year.
Petitioner is the sole breadwinner of the family, he has no other criminal antecedents.
Accordingly, she prays to allow the petition.
6. Per contra, learned HCGP and learned counsel for respondent No.2/victim have opposed the prayer made by the petitioner in the bail petition.

They submit that the petitioner, who was the coach of the victim girl, had taken NC: 2024:KHC:37350 advantage of his position and had committed heinous offence against the victim girl when she was a minor.

They submit that the petitioner's mobile phone contained nude photographs of the victim girl, and since the petitioner was continuously intimidating the victim girl, she had not approached the police.
Learned counsel for respondent No.2/victim submits that only with the assistance of the present coach the victim girl had subsequently approached the police and submitted her first information.
They submit that in the event the petitioner is enlarged on bail, he is likely to threaten the victim and other material witnesses.
Accordingly, they pray to dismiss the petition.

7. From the perusal of the typed first information dated 28.12.2023 submitted by the victim girl, it is seen that the date of birth of the victim girl is 28.04.2005 and she has been undergoing training in Sports Authority of India since 2020 and the petitioner is said to be her coach since then.
It appears that in the month of December- NC: 2024:KHC:37350 2022, the petitioner had left the Sports Authority of India since his contract period was over.

8. It is averred in the first information that even after that the victim girl was taking his assistance,
and in the second week of March-2023, when the victim girl had visited his house seeking his assistance for relaxation of her muscle, the petitioner allegedly had sexual intercourse with her against her wishes.

It is further alleged that thereafter he was threatening her, stating that he would circulate her personal photographs and videographs that he had in his mobile phone and he allegedly had taken her to a lodge at Koramangala in the month of May-2023 and had sexual intercourse with her.
She has stated that on 26.12.2023 she had brought this aspect of the matter to the notice of her present coach Sureshkumar, and thereafter, with his help, she had approached the police on 28.12.2023.

9. Perusal of the first information would go to show that there is no such allegation in the first information that NC: 2024:KHC:37350 from the year 2020 till the month of December-2022, the petitioner had taken any personal or obscene photographs or videographs of the victim girl in his mobile phone.
Undisputedly, the petitioner had left the Sport Authority of India in the month of December-2022.

sentences.text: 3 10. Allegation in the first information is that during the second week of March 2023 the victim girl had gone to the house of the petitioner for seeking his assistance for her muscle relaxation, and during the said period he had sexual intercourse with her against her wishes.
Except for the statement of the victim girl, at this stage there is absolutely no material to show that the victim girl had visited the petitioner's house during the third week of Decemeber-2023.
Subsequent allegations of sexual assault on the victim girl are all after she has attained the age of majority.

Even though it is seriously contended by the learned HCGP and learned counsel for respondent No.2, that the petitioner's mobile phone contained personal photographs and videographs of the victim girl, NC:
2024:KHC:37350 which were taken by him when she was a minor, there is no allegation in the first information that prior to March- 2023, at any point of time, the petitioner had taken the personal or obscene photographs or videographs of the victim girl.
The only allegation against the petitioner in the first information, which relates to the period prior to December-2022 is that he had kissed victim in the month of October-2022.

10. Learned counsel for the petitioner has stated that photographs and videographs of the victim found in the mobile phone of the petitioner were all forwarded by the victim and not captured or recorded by the petitioner in his mobile phone.
Material on record would go to show that the mobile phone of the victim girl has not been subjected to examination in the present case.

11. Learned counsel for the petitioner has produced medical documents of the petitioner's mother,
issued by the Bangalore Baptist Hospital, which prima facie would go to show that the petitioner's mother has been suffering NC: 2024:KHC:37350 from High Grade Serous Carcinoma Right Ovary and the Cancer is at III stage.
Medical records of the petitioner's mother would go to show that she was admitted in the hospital on a number of occasions and has already taken Chemotherapy treatment.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that except for the petitioner there is no other earning member in their family.
Petitioner who has no criminal antecedents, is in custody from 16.03.2024.
Investigation in the case is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
The allegation found in the charge sheet as against the petitioner is required to be proved in a full-fledged trial.
The victim girl has made allegation against the petitioner that he sexually assaulted her in the month of March-2023, but there is a delay of 9 months in submitting the first information.
Undisputedly, she had attained the age of majority in the month of April- 2023 and the present first information is filed in the month of December-2023.

Considering the aforesaid aspect of the matter, I am of the opinion that the petitioner's prayer for grant of regular bail needs to be answered affirmatively,
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:37350 without expressing any opinion on the merits/demerits of the case.

12. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Petition is allowed.
